name: Green-veg & chicken glass-noodle stir-fry — soy-free (clean sauce)

source.author: Hebrew recipe (screenshot), adapted to the user's real batches
source.notes: Soy-FREE ('clean sauce') green stir-fry — the user's adopted rotation main. Veg is flexible (whatever's on hand). Updated 2026-08-22 to the user's actual logged batch: 630 g chicken, 150 g dry glass noodles, 200 g broccoli, 2 zucchini, 100 g spinach, 8 mushrooms, ½ onion, 8 garlic, plus 1 tbsp soy sauce across the whole batch (so lightly seasoned, not strictly soy-free). No oil amounts were given — assumed ~1 tbsp sesame + ~1 tbsp frying oil. Each extra tbsp of oil ≈ +120 kcal / +14 g fat; tell me the real oil and I'll adjust.

serving_desc: ≈410 g cooked (batch ÷4). Logged batch: 630 g raw chicken + 150 g dry glass noodles

logged_instance.veg: 200 g broccoli, 2 zucchini, 100 g spinach, 8 mushrooms, ½ onion, 8 garlic
logged_instance.soy_sauce: 1 tbsp across the whole batch (~225 mg sodium/serving)
logged_instance.note: Made with mushrooms + onion in place of the original green beans / green onion / chili; a single tbsp of soy added for the batch.

steps: Sear chicken; stir-fry veg + noodles; fold spinach in at the end; finish with lemon.

batch_totals.note: Sodium ~1,540 mg batch (~385 mg/serving) — from the 1 tbsp soy added; far below the old 8-tbsp soy version.

him.verdict: Your best everyday cutting main. 40.8 g protein for ~445 kcal (~9 g protein per 100 kcal), lean, big green-veg volume, ~4 g fiber. The single tbsp of soy across the whole batch keeps sodium modest (~385 mg/serving) — a fraction of a fully soy-sauced stir-fry. Broccoli + spinach bring folate/vitamin C, mushrooms add selenium (a sperm micro). Only fat lever is the oil (~11 g/serving from sesame + frying oil). Glass noodles are the one refined carb, well balanced.
flags: modest sodium (~385 mg — just 1 tbsp soy in the batch)
fat driven by oil — the only lever
suggested_mods: 1 tbsp soy for the whole batch is a smart amount — keeps flavor without the sodium hit of a full-soy stir-fry
Measure/limit the oil — each tbsp is ~120 kcal; ~1 tbsp total is plenty in a nonstick

her_preconception.verdict: The best preconception main in the rotation. Spinach + broccoli make it a real FOLATE dish (~65 mcg DFE/serving, the #1 preconception nutrient), with iron (~2.7 mg) paired with the veg's vitamin C for absorption, plus choline and selenium on lean protein. Fully cooked, no sprouts, no high-mercury fish — no safety flags. Sodium is modest (~385 mg) with just the 1 tbsp soy; easy to keep there.
prenatal_highlights: folate from spinach + broccoli (~65 mcg DFE/serving) — top preconception nutrient
iron (~2.7 mg) paired with vitamin C for absorption
choline + selenium; lean protein; modest sodium (~385 mg)
suggested_mods: Fold the spinach in at the very end so the folate isn't cooked out
1 tbsp soy across the batch keeps sodium in a good place — use low-sodium soy if you want it even lower

adopted_note: Adopted rotation main (best-scoring + best preconception dish). Veg-flexible — make it with whatever green veg is on hand. Current logged batch (2026-08-22): 630 g chicken / 150 g dry glass noodles / broccoli + zucchini + spinach + mushroom + onion + 1 tbsp soy across the batch → ~445 kcal, 40.8 g protein, ~385 mg sodium per ~410 g serving (batch ÷4). Scales with chicken weight.
cooking_guide: Prep everything first — stir-fry moves fast. Soak the glass noodles in warm water until pliable (5-10 min), drain, and snip shorter with scissors.
Steam or blanch the broccoli ~2 min (it's the densest veg), then drain — this cooks it evenly and keeps it bright and crisp-tender.
Pat the chicken strips dry and season lightly. Heat the pan/wok hot before the oil goes in — high heat sears, low heat steams.
Stir-fry the chicken in a single layer until just cooked, then remove (crowding makes it grey and watery).
Stir-fry the garlic and onion briefly, then the mushrooms — leave the mushrooms undisturbed ~1 min to brown (moving them too soon makes them release water and steam).
Add the zucchini and blanched broccoli and toss 2-3 min to keep them crisp-tender.
Return the chicken, add the noodles with a splash of water, the sesame oil and 1 tbsp soy sauce; toss 1-2 min to combine and heat through (taste before adding any more salt).
Fold in the spinach at the very end and toss just until wilted — seconds only; overcooking dulls it and loses folate.
Finish off the heat with a squeeze of lemon or lime — it brightens everything and boosts iron absorption. Serve promptly.
